citations.quote: Among the 168 patients randomized to receive vorasidenib on the treatment arm of the INDIGO trial, a 16-month improvement in median PFS was observed in patients on the vorasidenib arm, with a median PFS of 27.7 months (95% CI: 17, NE) compared to 11.1 months (95% CI: 11, 13.7) for the placebo arm. The hazard ratio (HR) for PFS was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.27, 0.56; p-value <0.0001). There was also a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in the key secondary endpoint of TTNI for patients on the vorasidenib arm compared to the placebo arm with a HR of 0.26 (95% CI: 0.15, 0.43; p-value of < 0.0001). Median TTNI was not reached for the treatment arm and was 17.8 months for patients on the placebo arm.

key_safety.text: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 9% of patients. Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions were fatigue (33%), headache (28%), COVID-19 (28%), musculoskeletal pain (24%), diarrhea (21%), nausea (20%), seizure (16%), and dizziness (14%). Most common Grade 3/4 lab abnormalities were increased ALT (9%), increased AST (4.8%), increased GGT (2.2%), and decreased neutrophils (2.2%).

citations.quote: In the pooled safety population, serious adverse reactions occurred in 9% of patients receiving vorasidenib. The most common (\ge 15\%) adverse reactions were fatigue (33%), headache (28%), COVID-19 (28%), musculoskeletal pain (24%), diarrhea (21%), nausea (20%), seizure (16%), and dizziness (14%). The most common (\ge 2\%) Grade 3 or 4 laboratory abnormalities were increased ALT (9%), increased AST (4.8%), increased GGT (2.2%), and decreased neutrophils (2.2%).
